accuracy.evidence: Recomputed every number in the lab, items and challenge: 46 + 37 = 70 + 13 = 83; 68 + 29 = 98 − 1 = 97; 83 − 19 = 63 + 1 = 64; 91 − 87 = 4 (87→90 is 3, 90→91 is 1); 72 − 68 = 4; 83 − 25 = 58 and 62 + 25 = 87; 54 − 27 = 27; 57 + 38 = 95; 57 + 39 = 96; 73 − 68 = 5; sorter: 64 − 28 = 36, 52 − 17 = 35, 75 − 38 = 37 (so 44, 45, 43 are the slips), 70 − 36 = 34, 91 − 46 = 45. Strategy names checked against CCSS 2.NBT.5 and the NC Year 2/3 mental calculation guidance.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented two-digit errors: dropping the extra ten from the ones total (46 + 37 = 73, prediction 1, tag lostten), concatenating partial totals (713, tag glue), compensating the wrong way (68 + 29 = 99, 83 − 19 = 62, predictions 2 and 3, tag wrongway), smaller-from-larger digit subtraction (83 − 25 = 62, 54 − 27 = 33, sorter slips 44/45/43, tag flip), slow counting in ones for close numbers (tag slow) and a wrong inverse check (83 + 25, tag inv).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagflu100 is about choosing among strategies: part tiles dragged into Tens/Ones trays, tappable +30/−20 jump chips with a ±1 correction that turns red when it goes the wrong way, a counting-up dot between two close numbers, a strategy sort (Split / Round / Count up), and an inverse check that turns Sam's 62 into 87 ≠ 83 before the learner drags to 58. flagadd100 bridges a 2-digit number plus ones; flagregroup is the column method; the distinct gate passed under 30% against every lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner meets each idea before the text names it: the Ones tray shows 6 + 7 = 13 and the total only becomes 83 once both trays are full; tapping +1 after +30 shows 99 in red with 'adding 1 more makes it worse'; the counting-up hops show +3 then +1; the sorted bins end up grouped by number features; the inverse check makes the slip visible as 87 ≠ 83.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions with tempting wrong options: 'the 70s: 4 tens and 3 tens make 7 tens' (lost ten), 'add 1 more' after +30, 'take 1 more away' after −20 (wrong-way compensation), and 'yes' to Sam's 83 − 25 = 62. Each is tested by the task straight after and the reveal names the correct option.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven rotating questions with tagged wrong answers: lostten ('That extra ten must join the tens'), glue ('Do not write the tens total and ones total side by side'), wrongway ('Adjust the other way to undo the extra 1'), flip ('You took the smaller ones digit from the bigger one'), slow and inv, each naming the slip rather than just saying wrong.

readability.evidence: validate_lessons passes the family kid and adult limits. Kid text uses short sentences with concrete sums ('29 is one less than 30. So 68 + 29 is 68 + 30, take 1 away.'). Curriculum terms partition, compensation, difference, counting up and inverse are named in the adult text and shown in the lab.

no_filler.evidence: Four kid paragraphs: look first and split, round and adjust, count up, check by adding back. Adult: standards and key words, what fluency means and why each strategy works, five named mistakes, then exactly what the lab does. Filler and 12% overlap gates passed against the add-within-100, within-20 and within-1000 lessons.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px Android dark and iPhone 13 light after Show me on every step. Fixed after the first pass: the −20 label collided with the result line in 83 − 19 (both big jumps now arc above, the ±1 arc sits below unlabelled and the running sum '63 + 1 = 64' is printed under the line), and the gap step labels every tick so 87 and 91 are readable.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button twin: '40 → tens' / '40 → ones' per tile, '+ 30', '+ 1', '− 1' jump buttons, 'Back one' / 'Up one' / 'Check the gap', one button per strategy labelled with the current sum, and 'One less' / 'One more' / 'Check with adding'. The canvas aria-label and live region carry every message; walk.cjs ran axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
